item.title: FDA MedWatch - All Lots and Varieties of Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars by Once Upon A Farm
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

TOPIC: All Lots and Varieties of Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars by Once Upon A Farm: Recall - Due to Potential Choking Hazard

AUDIENCE: Consumer, Patient, Health Care Professional, Pediatrics, Emergency Medicine

ISSUE: Once Upon a Farm is recalling all lots and varieties of fruit-flavored Tractor Wheel Organic Toddler Soft-Baked bars due to reports that the composition of the Tractor Wheel toddler snack can rapidly hydrate into a dense, dry, and sticky mass upon contact with saliva and during chewing, which can result in a potential choking hazard for toddlers for ages 1.5-2.5 years old.

The Tractor Wheels were distributed nationwide, including Puerto Rico, and reached consumers via online sales and retail stores. This recall covers all lot codes currently available in distribution, including expired products which may be on consumers' shelves. Applicable unexpired Best If Used by Dates are 10/30/2026 to 8/26/2027.

The decision to recall these products was based on three consumer complaints that were reported to the FDA for choking. The company is working with the FDA to make sure affected products are removed as the company works on reformulating and families have the information they need.

No injuries have been reported to date.

For more information about this recall, click on the red button "Read Recall" below.

BACKGROUND: The products being recalled are sold as organic toddler soft-baked bars.

RECOMMENDATIONS: 

  • Consumers who have purchased this recalled Once Upon A Farm Tractor Wheels product should not open the package or consume the products. Instead, they should return the product to the location of purchase for a full refund or contact care@uponafarm.com.

  • Consumers with questions should contact the company at care@uponafarm.com or call 1-888-983-1606. 

Health care professionals, consumers and patients are encouraged to report adverse events or side effects related to the use of these products to the FDA's MedWatch Safety Information and Adverse Event Reporting Program:

  • Complete and submit the report online.
  • Download the form or call 1-800-332-1088 to request a reporting form, then complete it and return it to the address on form or submit it by fax to 1-800-FDA-0178.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Compact Medical Removes or Updates Instructions for ButterflyBVM
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Early Alert: Compact Medical Removes and Updates Use Instructions for ButterflyBVM Bag-Valve-Mask Resuscitators

The FDA is aware that Compact Medical has issued an “Urgent Medical Device Recall” notice to affected customers recommending certain lots of ButterflyBVM Single-Use Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM) Resuscitators be removed from where they are used or sold. The notice also recommends updated use instructions (correction) for certain lots prior to continued use.

Compact Medical has reported the potential for a hole to form in the bellows of certain ButterflyBVM devices. Units from Lots 000109 through 000117 have a higher rate of holes in the bellows than previously observed.

If a hole develops in the bellows, tidal volume can leak from the device instead of reaching the patient. A leak in the bellows can cause inadequate ventilation and hypoxia. If not corrected, this could result in serious injury or death.

As of November 2, 2026, Compact Medical has reported no serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

Read More

Questions?

Customers in the U.S. with adverse reactions, quality problems, or questions about this recall should contact Compact Medical at info@butterflybvm.com.

CDRH is issuing this Early Alert to notify the public of a potentially high-risk device issue. The FDA will keep the public informed and update this web page as significant new information becomes available.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - FDA Advises Consumers Not to Buy or Serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

TOPIC: FDA Advises Consumers Not to Buy or Serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars. Consumers Should Not Buy or Serve Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels, Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars Due to a Potentially Fatal Choking Hazard: FDA Safety Communication

AUDIENCE: Consumer, Patient, Health Care Professional, Pediatric

ISSUE: The FDA has received several reports that describe toddlers (ages 1.5–2.5 years) suffering complete airway obstruction with the inability to breathe after consuming the product. When chewed, the product reportedly forms a dry, sticky mass that standard choking interventions — including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver — may fail to dislodge. Some reported choking incidents have required emergency response intervention and hospital observation.

Stores affected: This product is sold nationwide online and at stores, including Costco, Target, and Walmart. This product may be sold elsewhere, such as Amazon.com and other third-party vendors. FDA will update this advisory as more information becomes available.

For more information about this alert, click on the red button "Read Alert" below.

BACKGROUND: The product included in this alert is sold as organic toddler soft-baked bars.

RECOMMENDATIONS: 

  • Consumers who have symptoms should contact their health care provider to report their symptoms and receive care.

  • Consumers should not buy or serve this product and should immediately throw it away.

  • Retailers should not sell this product.

  • Call 9-1-1 in the event that someone is choking and other first aid measures to dislodge the obstruction have failed.

[Posted 10/30/2026 - FDA Safety Communication]

To report a complaint or adverse event (illnesss or serious allergic reaction), visit Industry and Consumer Assistance.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Instrumentation Laboratories Removes HemosIL AcuStar HIT-IgG (PF4-H)
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) Radioimmunoassay Recall: Instrumentation Laboratories Removes HemosIL AcuStar HIT-IgG (PF4-H)

The FDA is aware that Instrumentation Laboratories (Werfen) has issued letters to affected customers recommending certain lots of HemosIL AcuStar HIT-IgG(PF4-H) be removed from where they are used or sold.

Instrumentation Laboratories (Werfen) stated that a performance issue has been identified affecting Lot No. B40005, B40006, B38062, and B38063 of HemosIL AcuStar HIT-IgG(PF4-H), Part No. 0009800127 and 0009802028. Customer complaints have reported obtaining an invalid calibration curve and in one complaint, a negative mean bias of 47% with patient samples. Werfen’s investigation has confirmed performance variability (negative bias of 20-35%) with the affected lots that may not be reliably detected through routine calibration and quality control testing. The root cause investigation is ongoing.

This performance issue may result in a negative bias that could cause sample results to be incorrectly reported below the assay cut-off (1.00 U/mL) and, therefore, be interpreted as “HIT IgG Antibody negative.” A false positive negative result may delay recognition of HIT and influence clinical management. In patients with HIT, continued exposure to heparin may increase the risk of thrombotic complications.

As of September 3, Instrumentation Laboratories (Werfen) has reported no serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

Read More

This recall involves removing certain devices from where they are used or sold. The FDA has identified this recall as the most serious type. This device may cause serious injury or death if you continue to use it.

Questions?

Customers in the U.S. with adverse reactions, quality problems, or questions about this recall should contact Werfen Client Services at 1-800-955-9525.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Medline Removes or Corrects All Medline Beds and Accessories
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Early Alert: Medline Removes or Corrects All Medline Brand Beds and Accessories  

The FDA is aware that Medline has issued an Urgent Medical Device Field Safety Notice notifying customers of the discontinuation and market exit of all Medline Brand beds and their associated pendants, accessories, replacement parts, and bed-containing order packages. Medline recommends these products be removed from where they are used or sold, or in some cases, corrected prior to continued use. 

All Medline Brand beds and associated components are affected by this action, including: 

  • Homecare Beds 
  • Bariatric Beds 
  • Long-term Care Beds  
  • Pendants 
  • Accessories 
  • Replacement Parts 
  • Bed-Containing Order Packages   

Medline has identified a potential fire hazard involving Medline Brand beds, hand-control pendants, control/motor boxes, and actuators/motors. Under certain conditions, including but not limited to excessive system loading, jammed components or motors, damage to or fluid ingress into the pendant, the use of extension cords, or the use of non-Medline or unapproved pendants or accessories, the bed's electrical components may overheat. 

Overheating of the bed's electrical components may progress to smoking, sparking, melting, burning, and/or fire. These events may increase the risk of adverse health consequences, including electrical shock and burns. If a fire occurs, there is the potential for serious injury or death, including burns, chronic respiratory conditions resulting from smoke inhalation, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) related to fire incidents, or fatality. Medline has received reports of adverse events associated with this issue. 

Medline has received information through post-market surveillance regarding risk when using any bed accessories. Specifically, the use of bed accessories may lead to entrapment. 

There is a potential risk of entrapment or asphyxiation if: 1) Medline Brand beds are used with any bed accessories, 2) if a user lays on a pendant being used with the bed, or 3) if the bed is used with loose or wobbly rails. Entrapment or asphyxiation may result in patient injury or death. Medline has received reports of adverse events associated with this issue. 

As of October 20, 2026, Medline has reported two deaths and 16 serious injuries associated with these issues. 

Read More

Questions?

Customers in the U.S. with questions about this recall should contact Medline Recall Customer Service at 800-950-0128, option 7. 

CDRH is issuing this Early Alert to notify the public of a potentially high-risk device issue. The FDA will keep the public informed and update this web page as significant new information becomes available.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Early Alert: B. Braun Removes Streamline Bloodline Set for Dialog+
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Early Alert: B. Braun Removes Streamline Bloodline Set for Dialog+  

The FDA is aware that B. Braun has issued a letter to affected customers recommending certain Hemodialysis Bloodlines be removed from where they are used or sold. Affected devices:  

  • Product Description: Streamline Bloodline Set for Dialog+  
  • Model: SL-2010M2096 
  • UDI-DI: 04046964367786; 04046964367779 
  • Impacted Lots: A2600099, A2600128, A2600136 

B. Braun stated that the required solvent application step during assembly was not performed, resulting in inadequate bonding of the dialyzer connector. As a result, the bloodline connector may detach or leak during priming or dialysis treatment, potentially leading to blood loss, clotting and occlusion of the extracorporeal circuit, and/or air ingress into the blood circuit. 

As of October 10, 2026, B. Braun has reported no serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue. 

Read More

Questions?

Customers in the U.S. with questions about this recall should contact B. Braun at recalls@bbraunusa.com or (610) 849-1197.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Ultimate Forza Male Supplement by Tonight We Ride
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

TOPIC: Ultimate Forza Male Supplement by Tonight We Ride: Recall - Due to Presence of Undeclared Sildenafil, Tadalafil, and Dapoxetine

AUDIENCE: Consumer, Patient, Health Care Professional, Cardiology

ISSUE: Tonight We Ride is recalling all lots of Ultimate Forza Male Supplement capsules because it has been found to contain undeclared Sildenafil, Tadalafil, and Dapoxetine.

The presence of Sildenafil, Tadalafil, and Dapoxetine in this product renders them unapproved drugs for which the safety and efficacy have not been established.

Sildenafil and Tadalafil are active ingredients in FDA-approved prescription drugs Viagra and Cialis, respectively, used to treat erectile dysfunction. FDA approval of Viagra and Cialis is restricted to use under the supervision of a licensed health care professional. These undeclared ingredients may interact with nitrates found in some prescription drugs, such as nitroglycerin, and may lower blood pressure to dangerous levels. People with diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or heart disease often take nitrates.

Dapoxetine is an active ingredient not approved by the U.S. FDA and therefore its safety or efficacy has not been established. Chemically, dapoxetine belongs to a class of drugs known as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) used to treat depression. Consumption has been shown to increase the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults.

No adverse events or complaints have been reported to date.

For more information about this recall, click on the red button "Read Recall" below.

BACKGROUND: Ultimate Forza Male Supplement capsules are marketed as male performance dietary supplements. 

RECOMMENDATIONS: 

  • Consumers should stop using Ultimate Forza Male Supplement immediately.

  • Consumers should contact their physician or healthcare provider if they have experienced any problems that may be related to taking or using this product.

  • Consumers may return unopened or partially used product to a GNC store for a full refund. A receipt or the phone number or email address associated with the loyalty account used for the purchase should be provided so the purchase can be verified.

  • Consumers with questions may contact the company at 1-877-462-4700 or GNCRecalls@gnc-hq.com.

Health care professionals, consumers, and patients are encouraged to report adverse events or side effects related to the use of these products to the FDA's MedWatch Safety Information and Adverse Event Reporting Program:

  • Complete and submit the report online.
  • Download the form or call 1-800-332-1088 to request a reporting form, then complete it and return it to the address on the form or submit it by fax to 1-800-FDA-0178.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Early Alert: Cardinal Health Updates Use Instructions for Presource Packs
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Early Alert: Cardinal Health Updates Use Instructions for Presource Packs Containing BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets 

The FDA is aware that Cardinal Health has issued a letter to affected customers recommending updated use instructions for convenience kits containing infusion sets affected by the BD and CareFusion BD Alaris Pump Infusion Set Recall. 

BD stated that some Alaris Pump sets with restrictive components and designs (such as closed male luer, filters, check valves, Y-sites, microbore tubing, etc.) perform worse than previously disclosed. The deviations most commonly occur at low programmable rates under 1 mL/h and at or under 5 mL of “bolus volume”. 

BD has continued to test BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets to update infusion set performance data for accuracy. This testing found that the previously claimed performance was overestimated, and, in some instances, the infusion performance is significantly worse. 

Performance attributes that differ from previously communicated values have the potential to result in greater degrees of under- or over-infusion, delayed time to occlusion alarms, and bolus dose inaccuracies. These examples of performance issues may not be readily detected by users. 

The severity and nature of the outcomes resulting from this communicated performance depend on various factors but, for the most vulnerable, high-risk populations (i.e., neonates, pediatrics, critically ill patients), could result in serious adverse events or death, as these higher risk patients are more likely to receive lower rate and/or lower volume infusions, such as antiarrhythmics or blood-pressure supporting medications. 

As of August 19, 2026, BD has not reported any serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue. 

Read More

Questions?

Customers in the U.S. with questions about this recall should contact their Cardinal Health sales representative.

CDRH is issuing this Early Alert to notify the public of a potentially high-risk device issue. The FDA will keep the public informed and update this web page as significant new information becomes available.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Nova Biomedical Removes StatStrip Glucose Hospital Meter Systems
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Hospital Glucose Meter Recall: Nova Biomedical Removes StatStrip Glucose Hospital Meter Systems

The FDA is aware that Nova Biomedical has issued a letter to affected customers recommending that all affected StatStrip Glucose Hospital Meters be removed from where they are used or sold until a software update becomes available. This removal only applies to the most recent model of the StatStrip Glucose Hospital Monitoring System, the “Gen 2.0” model, and does NOT apply to any previously released model of the StatStrip Glucose Hospital Meter System such as the “Gen 1.86”.

Nova Biomedical stated the issue affects StatStrip Glucose Hospital Meter Systems (Gen 2.0) operating on all versions of firmware and does not impact the analytical performance of glucose measurements.

Nova Biomedical has received reports from customers indicating that when scanning patient ID or Quality Control (QC) barcodes, prior information may remain on the meter screen, which if accepted, will lead to a glucose result being assigned to the wrong patient’s medical record or QC ID. If not recognized, healthcare providers may make clinical decisions based on another patient’s glucose result, potentially leading to delayed treatment, unnecessary treatment (including inappropriate insulin administration), and/or failure to treat the intended patient. The severity of harm depends on the patient’s actual glucose status and clinical condition. Critically ill patients and infants, who may be unable to communicate symptoms of hypoglycemia, are at greater risk of adverse outcomes.

As of October 5, 2026 Nova Biomedical has reported one serious injury and no deaths associated with this issue.

Read More

This recall involves removing certain devices from where they are used or sold. The FDA has identified this recall as the most serious type. This device may cause serious injury or death if you continue to use it.

Early Alert: Transcatheter Mitral Valve Delivery System Issue from Edwards Lifesciences

The FDA is aware that Edwards Lifesciences has issued a letter to affected customers recommending certain delivery systems used for SAPIEN M3 transcatheter mitral valve replacement be removed from where they are used or sold. Affected devices:

  • Commander M delivery systems (for SAPIEN M3 Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement System)
    • Lots: 67718561, 67804014, 67887043, and 67887044

Edwards Lifesciences stated it has received three reports of balloons bursting during inflation. Potential injuries associated with balloon burst include embolism and inability to retrieve the device through the guide sheath, which may require additional intervention, including surgery. Because this patient population is deemed unsuitable for surgery, these interventions carry a high risk of serious adverse health consequences including death.

As of October 5, Edwards Lifesciences has reported one death and one serious injury associated with this issue.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Argatroban Injection by Par Health
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

TOPIC: Argatroban Injection by Par Health: Recall - Due to the Presence of Particulate Matter

AUDIENCE: Patient, Health Care Professional, Risk Manager, Pharmacy, Cardiology, Hematology, Pulmonology

ISSUE: Par Health is recalling 22 lots of Argatroban Injection 250 mg/2.5 mL (100 mg/mL) to the hospital/user level due to the presence of particulate matter, identified as cellulose, polystyrene, polyethylene terephthalate, stopper material, and possibly stainless steel, that was detected in certain lots.

Administration of Argatroban Injection 250 mg/2.5 mL (100 mg/mL) found to contain particulate matter, has a reasonable probability of causing life-threatening adverse health consequences including pulmonary emboli (blockage in pulmonary blood vessels), occlusions of other blood vessels (which can lead to tissue death and possible organ damage), and/or inflammation of the walls of veins, which may lead to clotting.

The lots were distributed nationwide to wholesalers and hospitals between December 30, 2024, and May 5, 2026.

To date, Par Health has not received any reports of adverse events related to this recall.

For more information about this recall, click on the red button "Read Recall" below.

BACKGROUND: Argatroban Injection 250 mg/2.5 mL (100 mg/mL) is a direct thrombin inhibitor indicated for prophylaxis or treatment of thrombosis in adult patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and as an anticoagulant in adult patients with or at risk for HIT undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.

RECOMMENDATIONS: 

  • Wholesale distributors and hospital pharmacies that have the product being recalled should immediately discontinue use and stop distribution. If you have further distributed the recalled product, please notify your accounts or any additional locations which may have received the recalled product.

  • Questions regarding this recall can be directed to the company at 1-855-648-7909 or by email at rxrecalls@inmar.com.

  • For medical or technical product information or to report a product complaint or adverse event please call 1-800-828-9393.

item.title: FDA MedWatch - Early Alert: Diagnostic Ultrasound System Issue from Philips
item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

Early Alert: Diagnostic Ultrasound System Issue from Philips Ultrasound

The FDA is aware that Philips Ultrasound has issued a letter to affected customers recommending all Lumify diagnostic ultrasound systems have updated use instructions.  

Philips Ultrasound stated that due to a software issue, the Lumify Android or iOS application used with its ultrasound transducers may not recognize a previously registered transducer and will prompt users for re-registration without warning prior to point-of-care use. Scanning functionality is prevented until the registration step has been completed. Registration requires Wi-Fi or cellular signal access. 

Lumify devices used outside the hospital, such as in ambulances, aircraft, or field settings, are at greater risk due to more limited access to Wi-Fi/cellular signals. Philips has received reports that the unexpected re-registration events have prevented scanning in pre-hospital environments and delayed care to patients. These pre-hospital events occurred outside of Wi-Fi or cellular access. 

Additionally, Philips reported that the connection between the Lumify transducer USB cable to a customer’s tablet or phone may disconnect or have an unstable connection during use, which may disrupt continuous function of the device and result in a delay of care. 

Loss of functionality or system failure during a procedure may result in a delay in diagnosis and/or treatment. Because the Lumify system is intended for point-of-care use, where ultrasound imaging supports rapid diagnosis and treatment; real-time decision-making; triage of unstable patients; and access to diagnostic capabilities in mobile, underserved, or remote settings, loss of functionality or system failure may have greater consequences than with traditional ultrasound devices. Depending on the clinical situation and patient condition, delays in diagnosis or treatment could lead to serious injury or death. 

As of September 29, 2026, Philips Ultrasound has reported eight serious injuries and four deaths associated with this issue.

Infusion Set Recall: BD and CareFusion 303, Inc. Remove BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets

The FDA is updating the communication “Infusion Set Recall: BD and CareFusion 303, Inc. Remove BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets” to notify the public that BD and its subsidiary CareFusion have issued an updated letter notifying affected customers of worse performance, under certain use cases, for the BD Alaris Pump Module model 8100. Due to the difficulty in recognizing these performance issues, users may fail to identify them as the cause of clinically significant changes in a patient’s condition. The letter also provides updates regarding the removal and discontinuation of certain BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets.

The performance data and information in this letter replaces information previously communicated in BD field action MMS-25-5311.

Affected devices:

  • Product Description: BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets compatible with BD Alaris Pump Module Model 8100
  • Software: BD Alaris with Guardrails Suite MX, versions up to v.12.6

BD stated that some Alaris Pump sets with restrictive components and designs (such as closed male luer, filters, check valves, Y-sites, microbore tubing, etc.) perform worse than previously disclosed. The deviations most commonly occur at low programmable rates under 1 mL/h and at or under 5 mL of “bolus volume”.

BD has continued to test BD Alaris Pump Infusion Sets to update infusion set performance data for accuracy. This testing found that the previously claimed performance was overestimated, and, in some instances, the infusion performance is significantly worse.

As of August 19, 2026, BD has not reported any serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

IV Tubing Set Correction: ICU Medical Updates Use Instructions for IV Tubing Sets

The FDA is aware that ICU Medical has issued a customer communication recommending updated use instructions for certain IV tubing sets.

Affected products:

  • Plum Administration Sets with drip chambers
  • IV Non-Dedicated Gravity Administration Sets with drip chambers
  • IV Sets with drip chambers
  • Oncology Sets with drip chambers

In May 2026, ICU Medical received reports of small black specks and discoloration observed on the inner wall of drip chambers, as well as particulate matter found within the drip chambers in certain IV tubing sets. The concern involved black specks and particulate matter within the drip chamber wall, raising questions about whether these findings represent biological contamination or could enter the fluid path and pose a risk to patients.

ICU Medical conducted an investigation that included evaluation of returned samples, laboratory analysis, simulated-use testing, and inspection of product inventory, and has determined that the reported discoloration is intrinsic to the PVC used to manufacture the drip chamber and remains embedded within the drip chamber wall. The investigation demonstrated that the reported observations represent discoloration of the drip chamber material itself and the discolorations:

  • Are not biological contamination
  • Are not foreign material
  • Do not enter the fluid path
  • Do not dislodge under expected use conditions
  • Do not affect the structural integrity or performance of the drip chamber

ICU Medical has completed its investigation of reported discoloration observed in certain IV tubing set drip chambers. Based on this investigation, the observed discoloration is characteristic of the drip chamber material, does not enter the fluid path, and does not affect device safety, performance, or intended use.

Given these findings, ICU Medical no longer recommends the enhanced inspection activities described in prior communications. Products should continue to be used as intended and per facility protocol.

The investigation did not identify direct patient risk associated with use of affected products. In some circumstances, a healthcare provider who observes discoloration may elect to replace a product before use, which could result in a delay in therapy. These delays could be clinically significant, especially for time-sensitive, life-saving infusions or when a replacement cannot be readily obtained.

As of July 16, ICU Medical has not reported any serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

Read More

The affected products and recommendations for what to do with the devices in this communication have changed. The FDA has since determined that this device may cause temporary or reversible health problems, or—though unlikely—serious health problems.

item.description:
If your email program has trouble displaying this email, view as a webpage.

 Early Alert: Ventilator Issue from React Health

The FDA is aware that Ventec Life Systems Inc., doing business as React Health, has issued a letter to affected customers recommending updated use instructions and inspection procedures for all VOCSN ventilator devices with serial numbers 112786 and higher.  

React Health stated that the internal flow transducer (IFT) cable connector on VOCSN ventilator devices may become partially or fully unseated and result in loss of communication with the internal flow transducer board. This condition can lead to device reboots and recurring System Fault 10 alarms.  

This issue affects all VOCSN device configurations. The affected internal flow transducer cable is used across all device models identified in this communication, regardless of the enabled therapy configuration. No instances of reboots occurring while a patient was receiving ventilation therapy have been reported. Based on the available complaint and investigation data, the probability of an IFT-related reboot occurring while the device is actively providing ventilation therapy is considered remote. 

If a reboot were to occur while a patient is receiving ventilation therapy, the device will alarm (such as System Fault 10) and ventilation therapy from the affected VOCSN device will be interrupted. A therapy interruption could result in delay of therapy and/or a serious adverse event (depending on the patient's condition). Patients who are unable to sustain adequate spontaneous ventilation are particularly vulnerable; any interruption in therapy without the prompt initiation of alternative ventilatory support significantly increases the risk of serious injury, permanent impairment, or death, and may require immediate medical intervention to prevent irreversible harm. 

As of August 12, 2026, React Health has not reported any serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

Early Alert: Heart Pump Controller Issue from Abiomed

The FDA is aware that Abiomed has issued a letter to affected customers recommending certain Automated Impella Controllers (AIC) be removed from where they are used or sold. While awaiting service from Abiomed, hospital inventory can continue to be used to ensure continuity of care.

 Abiomed stated that a retrospective review of servicing records identified certain Impella Controllers that require hardware, firmware, and/or software updates to address quality issues with the potential for safety implications. These quality issues include a potential failure of the AIC to recognize the purge cassette during setup or change; a sticking, unreliable button that could impact the operator’s ability to select and confirm menu entries and possible loss of control of the console; an instability that could result in start-up failure; and other software defects. Without the hardware, firmware, and/or software updates, patients could face various problems such as delay of therapy, inadequate or loss of hemodynamic result, and other serious issues.

As of September 8, 2026, Abiomed has reported no serious injuries or deaths associated with this issue.

ISSUE: Global Mix is recalling niwali Tejocote Capsules (90 capsules, Herbal Supplement) and niwali Tejocote Pieces (90 Day Supply, Herbal Supplement) because FDA analysis has determined that the products appear to be Thevetia peruviana, or yellow oleander.
